clue.text: One lizard primarily lives in sun, like this tropical one?

definitions.text: One lizard primarily lives in sun, like this tropical one?

indicators.note: in says the first group of pieces sits inside the word for sunning oneself

parts.note: to sun oneself is to bask
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: primarily asks for the opening letter of the word lizard

parts.note: lives, as in exists, gives the verb is

explanation.surface: A puzzled naturalist wonders whether a lizard basking in the sun is one of the tropical kind.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: the basilisk is a tropical American lizard that does indeed bask.
explanation.definitionFit: The basilisk is a Central and South American lizard, famous for running across water, so it is exactly a tropical lizard.

clue.text: Back part of dress, not obvious when front half is reversed

indicators.note: the first three of the six letters of the synonym for not obvious are turned round, leaving the rest alone

parts.note: something subtle is not obvious

explanation.surface: A fashion note: the back of a dress can be discreet when its front is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A bustle is the padded framework worn at the rear of a Victorian dress to puff out the skirt behind.

clue.text: Endlessly keep prisoner in place of internment

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the synonym for keep is dropped

parts.note: to keep can mean to stay or remain
an old lag is slang for a convict

explanation.surface: Guards are told to hold a prisoner indefinitely in a detention camp.
explanation.walkthrough: LAG for a prisoner is British slang, as in 'old lag', a long-serving convict.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp, so it is a camp for interned captives.

clue.text: Someone not quite upright but more efficient?

definitions.meaning: a person who tilts or inclines away from the vertical
the comparative of lean, as in a slimmed-down, more efficient organisation

explanation.surface: An office appraisal: a slouching worker might yet be the more productive one.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a person who tilts; the other is the comparative of lean, meaning trimmed of waste and so more efficient.

clue.text: Trainee astronaut who keeps taking out-of-this-world trips?

definitions.meaning: literally a cadet training for space flight
an idiom for a dreamy, spaced-out person, with trips hinting at drug experiences

explanation.surface: A trainee astronaut keeps making journeys beyond the Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a cadet in space training; idiomatically, an absent-minded person whose mind seems to drift off elsewhere.

clue.text: Keeper fell, following selection for national team

indicators.note: following puts the hill word after the selection word

parts.note: a player picked for their country is awarded a cap
a fell is a hill in northern England, as is a tor, a rocky peak

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper takes a tumble just after being picked for his country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeper' and 'fell' both suggest a football goalkeeper falling; in fact fell is a noun, a hill, and keeper is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A captor is one who holds someone captive, a keeper in the sense of jailer.

clue.text: Inflammatory person unbalanced on stairs

indicators.note: unbalanced suggests the letters of on stairs lose their order and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A firebrand teeters unsteadily on a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally inflammatory: an arsonist is someone who sets fire to property deliberately.

clue.text: Pare zest twists in swingers' bars

indicators.note: twists signals that the letters of pare zest are wrung into a new order

explanation.surface: A cocktail recipe: pare the zest into twists for drinks in bars where swingers gather.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze is the bar on which circus acrobats swing, so these are bars for swingers.

clue.text: Lingerie's lingerie? Much of it's white

indicators.note: much of says the letters wanted are most of the run of the first two clue words, running across them

explanation.surface: A puzzled shopper asks about lingerie's own lingerie, noting most of it is white.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated word looks like nonsense or an anagram; it is just the text the answer sits inside, starting at the R of the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Riesling is a German grape and the white wine made from it, so it is a white.

clue.text: Boat propeller area in sweeping motion making rapid progress

indicators.note: in places the boat-propeller and area pieces inside the swinging word

parts.note: to sway is to move in a sweeping back-and-forth motion
an oar drives a rowing boat along

explanation.surface: A rower's oar sweeps through the water as the boat speeds ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Soaraway is an adjective for rapid, spectacular success, as in a soaraway bestseller.

clue.text: Southern capital included in Eastern European getaway

indicators.note: included in places the southern and capital pieces between the two E pieces

parts.note: a capital letter is often shortened to cap

explanation.surface: A southern capital city is folded into an Eastern European trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A getaway is a flight from captivity or danger, and an escape is the same thing.

clue.text: Prepared to rise and depart lair in turn

parts.note: to depart is to leave

indicators.note: in turn means the lair word is turned round

parts.note: a den is an animal's lair

explanation.surface: An animal gets ready to rise and quit its lair, one after another.
explanation.definitionFit: Dough that has been leavened has had yeast or raising agent added so that it will rise.

clue.text: Stop hiding backward place around Nevada

indicators.note: around says the turned place word wraps the state abbreviation
backward means the place word is read right to left

parts.note: lieu means place, as in 'in lieu of'
NV is the US postal abbreviation for Nevada

explanation.surface: Someone stops hiding out in a remote backwater of Nevada.
explanation.definitionFit: To unveil is to reveal or uncover, which is to stop concealing something.

clue.text: Border company with connections present global 50-per-cent share?

parts.note: a hem is the border of a garment
an ISP, internet service provider, is a company selling online connections
to be present is to be here

explanation.surface: A business offering a border and internet connections holds half the world's market.
explanation.definitionFit: A hemisphere is half of the globe, so it is a fifty-per-cent share of the world.

clue.text: Possibly Japanese patch with stone covered by unflowering plant

indicators.note: covered by places the patch and stone pieces inside the plant word

parts.note: a fern reproduces by spores and never flowers
a patch of ground is an area
ST abbreviates stone, the British unit of weight

explanation.surface: A Japanese garden: a stony patch overgrown by greenery that never blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Japan is in East Asia, so something Japanese is an example of something from that region.

clue.text: Leave problem with one of computer's arrow keys?

definitions.meaning: a British idiom for moving house or departing abruptly

definitions.text: problem with one of computer's arrow keys?

explanation.surface: A frustrated user wants to walk away from a keyboard with a jammed arrow key.
explanation.definitionFit: To up sticks is British slang for moving away; read literally, it says the upward arrow key is stuck.

clue.text: Inordinately proud to possess personal power shower?

indicators.note: to possess means the shuffled letters hold the personal word inside
inordinately signals the letters of proud are thrown out of order

parts.note: personal property is your own

explanation.surface: An excessively vain person has fitted a powerful shower of their own.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy burst of rain is jokingly a shower with real power behind it.

clue.text: Stuart reign's ending with King George installed as Scottish leader

indicators.note: installed puts the king and George pieces inside the other pieces

parts.note: Stu is a short form of the name Stuart

indicators.note: the ending of reign is its final letter

parts.note: R, for Rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A history lesson: the Stuart reign ends, King George is crowned head of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Stuarts and Hanoverian Georges suggest a monarch, but the leader is Nicola Sturgeon, then Scotland's First Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicola Sturgeon was First Minister of Scotland when this was set, so she was the Scottish leader.

clue.text: What could make hipsters so hip, say, if it's artificial?

definitions.text: What could make hipsters so hip, say, if it's artificial?

indicators.note: could make suggests the letters of hipsters so can be rebuilt into something else

explanation.surface: A wry question about what could make trendy young things fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: an artificial hip is one example of this device.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificial body part such as a replacement hip joint is a prosthesis.

clue.text: Composer more appropriate for radio?

indicators.note: for radio means the word is heard spoken rather than seen

parts.note: something more appropriate is more right, comparative righter

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a different composer would suit a broadcast better.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who composes words, letters or music is an author of them.

clue.text: Persistence of team in healthy years

indicators.note: in puts the team inside the healthy word

parts.note: fit means healthy
XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: A team keeps going over healthy years of play.
explanation.definitionFit: Fixity is the quality of being fixed and unchanging, which is a kind of persistence.

clue.text: Perfidious person, Liberal, going after women's facility

indicators.note: going after places the Liberal letter last

parts.note: W abbreviates women's, as on a toilet door
facility means ease, as in doing something with facility

explanation.surface: A treacherous Liberal politician heads for the ladies' toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Weasel is slang for a sly, untrustworthy person who betrays others.

clue.text: Tough guy's first off going over treeless plain

indicators.note: going over says the remaining letters are flipped right to left
first off means the opening letter of the tough-guy phrase is removed

parts.note: a hard nut is a tough person

explanation.surface: A tough man sets off across a bleak, treeless expanse.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is the vast, flat, treeless Arctic region where the subsoil is permanently frozen.

clue.text: Up for play but not up for helping with encouragement

indicators.note: but not means the following word is removed from the helping word

parts.note: to be supportive is to help with encouragement

explanation.surface: Someone is keen to join the game but not to cheer others on.
explanation.definitionFit: Sportive means playful or frolicsome, so ready and eager for play.

clue.text: Low-growing plant with chlorine in excess

parts.note: Cl is the chemical symbol for chlorine
over means in excess, as in over the limit

explanation.surface: A ground-cover plant has been given too much chlorine.
explanation.definitionFit: Clover is a low-growing leguminous plant with trefoil leaves, often found in lawns.

clue.text: Hipsters mostly tolerate having no money around

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the tolerate word is dropped

parts.note: to bear is to tolerate

indicators.note: around means the penniless word is turned back to front

parts.note: skint is British slang for penniless

explanation.surface: Trendy young people mostly put up with being broke.
explanation.walkthrough: SKINT is everyday British slang for having no money.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatniks were the bohemian young nonconformists of the 1950s Beat Generation, the original hipsters.

clue.text: Short grass skirts certainly not coming back as beachwear

indicators.note: coming back means the whole assembly is read in the opposite direction
skirts means the shortened grass word goes around the refusal
short means the last letter of the word grass is cut off

parts.note: no means certainly not

explanation.surface: Grass skirts are firmly off the menu as beachwear on the return trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skirts' is a verb meaning goes round, not the garment; 'Short' drops the last letter of grass and 'coming back' reverses the whole result.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarong is a length of cloth wrapped round the waist, often worn on the beach.

clue.text: Brawl in wood clearing

indicators.note: in puts the brawl word inside the wood word

parts.note: deal is pine or fir timber
a fray is a fight or brawl

explanation.surface: A fight breaks out in a clearing in the forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Defrayal is the paying off of costs, so it means the clearing of a debt or expense.
